# Theme contracts and provenance

## Device profiles1.1.0

- User clarified Minimalist-like Desktop/Mobile/iOS Mobile variants rather than requiring a separate dashboard. Inspected UI-Lovelace-Minimalist/UI themefiles and official card-mod README-themes: exact card-mod-theme name plus card-mod-root CSS. Device profiles add opt-in card-mod only; no copied Minimalist palette or new Orbit runtime.
- Inspected frontend hui-root.ts: direct wrapper div has edit-mode class, header contains native ha-icon-button-arrow-prev for subviews, next sibling hui-view-container#view owns header/safe-area padding. CSS matches that recognized shape, exempts edit/subview Back and uses a767px breakpoint. Unknown shape stays visible. This is a version-sensitive frontend implementation contract, not a stable HA theme API.
- Card-mod4.2.1 tag11005313b240da0f7880b95aedc5a9876c293b83: root patch firstUpdated→apply_card_mod(root), exact theme lookup from --card-mod-theme plus themes.themes, cm_update refresh. Real99,373-byte card-mod.js pinned by hash in optional browser test; neither dependency binary nor host paths shipped.
- Recovery is direct/profile card navigation to /profile then select Desktop/default before entering Edit. No unsupported ?edit query bypass promised. Native subview/back_path retained; see example dashboard. No forced separate dashboard, automatic OS/profile switching or global frontend.set_theme.

- [HA frontend theme format/modes/splitting/profile/reload](https://www.home-assistant.io/integrations/frontend/#defining-themes): one named mapping per theme, `modes.light`/`modes.dark`, quoted colors; modes layer over native defaults. Theme definitions are separate from Lovelace JS resources. Preserve/merge existing frontend settings and theme includes.
- [HACS theme repository requirements](https://www.hacs.xyz/docs/publish/theme/): one theme YAML under themes/ per Theme repository. This remains a **Dashboard plugin repository**, with one optional companion YAML/manual install; Dashboard HACS update is not claimed to copy or activate themes.
- Official frontend sources inspected before implementation: `src/resources/theme/color/color.globals.ts`, `color/semantic.globals.ts`, `typography.globals.ts`, `main.globals.ts`, and `src/components/ha-card.ts` (HA card background, border, radius, shadow). Legacy primary/text/sidebar/header/input/MDC variables and modern text/surface/form/fill/border aliases are explicit. Beyond documented primary/accent/state keys frontend variables can change across versions; unused modern aliases are harmless on older frontends. Suite minimum remains HA2026.6.0, not native-version certification.
- Three families are generated from `themes/palettes.json`; `scripts/themes.mjs` writes a single quoted-scalar YAML plus a JSON browser catalog. No added npm/runtime dependency. YAML syntax independently parsed using an available YAML library; token-pair contrast checked numerically.
- `scripts/theme-bridge.mjs` is a deterministic build-only transformation, guarded by `themes/bridge-contracts.json`. Base accent variables and exact decorative CSS selectors gain `var(--orbit-theme-*,original)` fallbacks. It does not mutate pinned files, change services/HTML/event handlers or inject runtime observers/global CSS. Explicit later palettes and state overrides retain precedence. Palette/metric information colors are not globally replaced.
- Six populated preview cards: Welcome, two Room instances, Weather bars, Media Player and Temperature/Humidity (five distinct card types). Baseline v1.8.0 and new no-theme computed colors/backgrounds/radius/shadow/geometry match. Matrix additionally mounts all28 primary types under six modes; placeholder mounts alone are not full visual/functional audits.
- Visual review caught full-inset pseudo-elements that must use a transparent overlay hook, not the narrow stripe gradient hook; protected by a regression. Initial test-only corrections: ready flag referenced through window before module completion; valid cold/warm threshold pair; first-selector boundary for the CSS bridge.
- Preview uses a synthetic HA-like navigation/form/dialog shell and local SVG icon stubs. Native HA/Companion, stock editors/dialogs and actual installed frontend theme loading are explicitly unverified; no production connector or live HA instance was used.
